item.title: The latest from Trump's press conference
item.description: President Trump gave a wide-ranging press conference following his historic trip to Asia where he met with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin.
item.content:encoded: President Trump gave a wide-ranging press conference following his historic trip to Asia where he met with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin.

item.title: A second judge blocks Trump's arch, saying it's unlikely to succeed in court
item.description: A federal judge in Virginia said she will issue a preliminary injunction against Trump's arch, going a step further than the D.C. federal judge who temporarily blocked construction earlier this week.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Trump initially accepted the midterm results, but most GOP voters doubt they were fair
item.description: Less than half of Republicans nationwide considered the midterm elections "free and fair," according to new polling.

item.title: Trump touts meeting with Xi and Putin but offers little results
item.description: At a White House press conference Friday, Trump offered little in actual results of the meetings, beyond a joint statement on unity over some issues.

item.title: Dems aim to block Iran war funding. And, Army delays lead azide detonation in Iowa
item.description: Congress needs to pass a funding measure to avoid a shutdown next month, providing Dems an opportunity to leverage power. And, the Army says waiting to detonate lead azide could become dangerous.

item.title: Senate passes bipartisan energy bill amid environmental concerns
item.description: As Americans struggle with rising energy costs and increased demand driven by AI, the Senate passed a bipartisan bill that will speed up the approval process for data centers and power plants.

item.title: New York City unveils a bold plan to move its jails off Rikers Island
item.description: New York City officials are moving forward with plans to close Rikers, the city's main jail complex, after years of discussion. The jail has been plagued by assaults and inmate deaths.

item.title: Judges have put Trump's arch and golf course on hold, but only for a matter of days
item.description: A federal judge has twice delayed construction of Trump's arch. Another is keeping East Potomac Park open. The proposed golf course redesign got mixed feedback from a federal arts panel on Thursday.
